title: Result-bearing loop machine
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Turing machines over Boolean words, let $q$ be a state of $B$, let $I$ be a predicate on pairs of Boolean words, let $u,A,o$ be functions on pairs of Boolean words, where $A$ is Boolean-valued and $o$ is word-valued, and let $s_0$ map Boolean words to Boolean words. Let $R,T : \\mathbb{N} \\to \\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $F$ computes the binary digits of $R(|x|)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps, $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds, and $I(x,s)$ implies $I(x,u(x,s))$. Suppose startup on each $x$ reaches the clean seam with word $s_0(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps without visiting $q$ earlier. For every $x,s$ with $I(x,s)$, suppose a round takes positive time at most $T(|x|)$ without an intermediate positive-time visit to $q$; if $A(x,s)$ holds, it halts with output $o(x,s)$, and otherwise it reaches the clean seam with word $u(x,s)$. Then there are a finite Turing machine $E$ and a natural number $c$ such that $E$ computes within $c(T(n)+1)(R(n)+2)$ steps the word $o(x,u^i(x,s_0(x)))$ for the least $i\\le R(|x|)$ with $A(x,u^i(x,s_0(x)))$, if such an index exists, and the empty word if none exists.
hypotheses_covered: $B,F$ are finite Turing machines over Boolean words
$I$ is a predicate on pairs of Boolean words
$u,A,o$ are functions on pairs of Boolean words; $A$ is Boolean-valued and $o$ is word-valued
$s_0$ maps Boolean words to Boolean words
$R,T$ map natural numbers to natural numbers
$F$ computes the binary digits of $R(|x|)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps
Startup on each $x$ reaches the clean seam with word $s_0(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps without an earlier visit to $q$

For every invariant pair $(x,s)$, a positive-time round of at most $T(|x|)$ steps avoids intermediate positive-time visits to $q$ and either halts with output $o(x,s)$ if $A(x,s)$ or reaches the clean seam with word $u(x,s)$ otherwise
replaced:
Let a loop body with anchor be given, a fuel machine computing the binary digits of
$R(|x|)$ in time $T$, an invariant that holds at the initial word and is preserved by
the step function, a bounded anchor-free startup, and a per-round contract in which an
accepting round halts with a declared payload word and a rejecting round advances to the
seam of the stepped word. Then there are a finite machine $E$ and a constant $c$ such
that $E$ computes, within $c (T(n) + 1)(R(n) + 2)$ steps on inputs of length $n$, the
payload of the first accepted orbit point among the first $R(|x|) + 1$ iterates of the
initial word, and the empty word when no orbit point is accepted.
